deep.reconstruction:
Context (pages 3-4): Grothendieck is axiomatizing a 'tame' geometry over a set R, presumably an ordered field such as the reals. The data are families M_n ⊂ P(R^n), one for each n ≥ 1. The axioms are stability under:
- coordinate permutations;
- the diagonal embedding R^n → R^{n+1} (pullback, and preimage along it);
- intersection with cylinders over sets in M_n;
- projections R^{n+1} → R^n.

The structure is functorial in maps of finite sets I → J, through R^J → R^I. The previous page reformulated the axioms M1–M3 in this functorial way and began removing degenerate cases:
- (*) M_1 ≠ ∅, since if one M_n is empty, all are.
- (**) ∅ ∈ M_1. Otherwise each M_n, being stable under finite intersections, is a filter base.

This page continues the case analysis:
1. Replacing M_n by M'_n = M_n ∪ {∅} preserves the axioms, so adjoining ∅ is harmless.
2. By M1, if M_n = {∅} for one n, then this holds for every n. That case is trivial (it satisfies the axioms) and is excluded by (***): there is a nonempty A ∈ M_1.
3. He extends the indexing to I = ∅ by setting M_∅ = P(R^∅) = {∅, {e}}, where R^∅ is a one-point set. He notes that the properties M'1 and M'4 remain valid when I or J is empty. This makes the structure a functor on all finite sets, empty set included, which is a Lawvere-theory or hyperdoctrine-like setup.
4. For x = (x_1, …, x_n) ∈ R^n, M1 and M4 give: {x} ∈ M_n iff {x_i} ∈ M_1 for every i. One direction is projection. The other writes {x} as the intersection of pulled-back singletons.
5. He defines R_0 = {x ∈ R : {x} ∈ M_1}, the set of 'definable points', and R_0^I = {x ∈ R^I : {x} ∈ M_I}. He then corrects R_0 ≠ ∅ to card R_0 ≥ 2 and observes: if card R_0 ≥ 2, the intersection of two distinct definable singletons is ∅, so ∅ ∈ M_1 and condition ③/(**) holds automatically.
6. Section ⑤ announces examples, excluding the trivial cases M_n = ∅ for all n and M_n = {∅} for all n.

This is foundational bookkeeping for a functorial axiomatics of 'tame' (o-minimal-type) structures, the programme sketched in Esquisse §5.
errors: Slip of the pen: '{x} ∈ R^n' should read '{x} ∈ M_n'.
The step 'if {x_i} ∈ M_1 for all i then {x} ∈ M_n' needs the full space R^n (or cylinders) to lie in M_n, or some product axiom. Presumably this is M4, which is not visible on these pages.
'si on pose pour I ≠ ∅' must logically mean I = ∅, since M_∅ is being defined. Either a misreading or a slip.
The original correction from R_0 ≠ ∅ to card R_0 ≥ 2 is right: a single definable point does not force ∅ ∈ M_1.

ideas.what: Functorial axiomatics of tame/definable sets indexed by finite sets I, with pullback, preimage and projection along maps of finite sets
ideas.modern_name: Structure in the sense of o-minimality (van den Dries); definable sets as a hyperdoctrine/Lawvere-type functor
ideas.usually_credited_to: van den Dries (1984, 1998 book), Pillay–Steinhorn (1986); hyperdoctrines: Lawvere (1969)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5 (only as a programme, without axioms)

ideas.what: Elimination of degenerate cases: M_n empty, M_n = {∅}, and M_n not containing ∅ (filter bases); adjoining ∅ preserves the axioms

ideas.modern_name: Nullary sorts / truth values in a hyperdoctrine

ideas.what: R_0, the set of points whose singleton belongs to M_1; a singleton {x} lies in M_n iff each coordinate singleton lies in M_1

missed.claim: This is Grothendieck's own attempt at axiomatizing tame topology as families of subsets of R^I, functorial in finite sets I. It parallels the later definition of o-minimal structures. The page itself contains only routine normalizations.
missed.quote: si on pose pour I=∅ M_∅ = P(R^∅) = {∅,{e}} ... les propriétés M'1, M'4 restent satisfaites
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Documents that Grothendieck independently formulated a definable-set axiomatics, in a categorical, finite-set-indexed form, close to van den Dries' structures. This is of historical interest only; nothing new mathematically.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is routine case-elimination in an axiom system. Its interest is purely historical: it shows Grothendieck's functorial axiomatics of tame structures, which was later developed independently as o-minimality.
transcription_corrections: '{x} ∈ R^n ⟺ ...' : the image reads {x} ∈ R^n, but M_n is intended.
'si on pose pour I ≠ ∅' should probably be 'I = ∅', given the definition of M_∅ that follows.
The marginal note reads roughly '(en prenant def) les propriétés M'1, M'4 (cf ①) restent satisfaites à la bonne ... I, J ≠ ∅ ...', i.e. the properties remain valid when I, J are allowed to be empty.
'donc on satisfait ③' refers to condition (**) from the previous page.
